why: A carmaker surveying 51,000 drivers (17,000 owners plus 34,000 others) is believable, and every rating distribution in the four charts adds to 100%.
A heritage railway collecting 2,600 reply cards in a month is believable, and both pies (45/40/15 and 80/15/5) add to 100%.
All four score distributions add to 100%, and 900 respondents being 18% of enrolment implies a campus of about 5,000 students, which suits a business school.
A city botanic garden gathering 3,900 exit replies over six weekends is believable, and both pies (40/45/15 and 70/20/10) add to 100%.
In-store tastings with 25,000 shoppers (9,000 plus 16,000) are believable for a drinks brand across many stores, and all eight rating distributions add to 100%.

Half-year revenue of $252 to $267 million matches over $500 million a year, about $175k of revenue per employee suits a uniform rental firm with 2,900 staff, and revenue times the margin index gives annual profit falling from 2008 to 2010 as stated.
Overseas market shares of 0.3% to 7.3% fit a firm that sells little abroad, and profit margins of 12% to 44% are high for paint but within a factor of a few of what it could report.

The potter numbers agree (0.5 plus 2 extra makes 2.5, and the step chart gives 0.5 potters for 31 bowls and 2.5 for 147), and about 2.5 hours per hand-thrown bowl is slow but within a factor of a few of a small studio's rate.
A rural racing circuit collecting 6,500 survey sheets over three meetings, with only 5% local spectators, is believable, and both pies add to 100%.
Profit equals revenue minus costs in both periods, the average days per month (30.3 and 30.6) match the calendar, and about $7 of revenue per case is believable for a bottler.
